Sample.evidence_source: The 35 interviews allowed us to explore previous suicide attempts in a group of offenders around the time of their release from a category B male prison.

Country.evidence_source: The generalisability is limited because the sample was drawn from a reception prison in South-West England.

Population.evidence_source: The 35 interviews allowed us to explore previous suicide attempts in a group of offenders around the time of their release from a category B male prison.

Type.evidence_source: The 35 interviews allowed us to explore previous suicide attempts in a group of offenders around the time of their release from a category B male prison. The 100% agreement to participate and the fact that a significant number were re-interviewed following release are strengths and suggest that offenders were positive about engaging in the research, thus limiting ethical concerns.

Area.evidence_source: It has been suggested that this group is at higher risk of suicide and self-harm than long-term prisoners because their short sentences mean that, when released, they do not fall under the supervision of the probation services and, therefore, do not benefit from post-release support (Pratt et al. 2006). Some, as we have seen, saw hope for the future as they approached release.
